Requested Procedure: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus)
CPT Code: 28296
Requesting Provider: Reyes, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)
Reference Number: POC-3F7F71F65B-18736
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-08

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal Aetna’s decision to deny prior authorization for my requested bunion surgery (CPT code 28296), which is scheduled to be performed by Dr. Reyes. The denial letter dated August 8, 2026, states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." However, a review of my clinical records and weight-bearing foot radiographs demonstrates that my imaging findings and clinical history fully satisfy the criteria set forth in Aetna's Clinical Policy Bulletin (CPB) 0629 ("Bunionectomy"). 

According to Aetna CPB 0629, a "Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older" is considered medically necessary when specific imaging and clinical thresholds are met.

My clinical presentation and diagnostic studies align perfectly with Aetna’s requirements as outlined below:

1. Imaging Findings (Directly addressing the denial reason)
Aetna's policy requires:
"Radiographic confirmation... of the most recent weight-bearing view X-ray demonstrating both of the following: An HVA of 30 degrees or greater; and An inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) (formed by the long axis of the first and second metatarsals) of 12 degrees or greater"

On June 23, 2026, I underwent weight-bearing foot radiographs. The official interpretation and report of these weight-bearing views documented:
- A hallux valgus angle (HVA) of 38 degrees (which exceeds Aetna’s requirement of 30 degrees or greater).
- An intermetatarsal angle (IMA) of 17 degrees (which exceeds Aetna’s requirement of 12 degrees or greater).

The policy also states: "Radiographic confirmation must include interpretation and report of weight bearing anterior/ posterior and lateral views of the affected foot." I have enclosed the complete radiology report from my June 23, 2026 imaging, which provides this exact confirmation.

2. Conservative Treatment History
Aetna’s policy requires documentation of persistent symptoms "despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional". My conservative treatment far exceeds this requirement:
- I have suffered from progressive foot pain for 14 months that is unrelieved by rest, making it impossible to tolerate closed shoes.
- I completed a 14-week course of conservative care under professional direction from March 21, 2026, to June 27, 2026, consisting of 24 physical therapy visits. This treatment included activity modification, custom orthotics, and wide toe-box footwear (as detailed in my enclosed physical therapy discharge note).
- I have utilized oral NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on April 14, 2026, which provided only 4 weeks of partial, temporary relief.

3. Secondary Clinical Criteria
Aetna’s policy requires that the member has "one or more of the following" clinical complications. My medical records document multiple indicators in this category:
- "Limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint": Dr. Reyes’s physical examination notes that my first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint range of motion is limited by pain, with positive provocative testing on the affected side.
- "Ulceration caused by bunion" (or risk thereof): My clinical records document a persistent ulceration risk over the medial bony prominence due to the severity of the joint deformity and my inability to tolerate closed footwear.

Furthermore, as an adult patient who has reached skeletal maturity, I meet the age and skeletal maturity requirements outlined in the policy. I am a non-smoker with a BMI of 29, have no active infections, and have no untreated substance use issues, making me an excellent candidate for this corrective procedure.

Given that my weight-bearing radiographs show an HVA of 38 degrees and an IMA of 17 degrees—both of which significantly exceed Aetna's requirements—and because I have failed over a year of conservative management, the requested procedure is medically necessary.

Please review the attached radiology reports, physical therapy records, and clinical notes from Dr. Reyes, and reverse this denial so that I may proceed with this medically necessary surgery.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Jordan Jennings

Enclosures:
1. Weight-bearing foot radiograph report (dated June 23, 2026)
2. Physical therapy discharge note (documenting 24 visits from March 21, 2026, to June 27, 2026)
3. Clinical evaluation and office notes from Reyes, MD
